facts.statement: The genus Kuiornis was described by Worthy and colleagues in 2010.
The only known species in the genus Kuiornis is Kuiornis indicator.
Kuiornis indicator is an extinct species of wren belonging to the family Acanthisittidae.
facts.quote: Kuiornis indicator is an extinct New Zealand wren (Acanthisittidae)

facts.statement: Fossils of Kuiornis indicator date to the early Miocene, between 19 and 16 million years ago, found in the St Bathans fauna of Central Otago.
facts.quote: known from the early Miocene (19–16 million years ago) St Bathans fauna in Central Otago

facts.statement: The species is known from a single fossil specimen, a holotype consisting of a proximal right tarsometatarsus.
facts.quote: It is known from a holotype proximal right tarsometatarsus (NMNZ S.50929)

facts.statement: The time range for the genus Kuiornis is estimated from 18.7 to 15.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Burdigalian to Langhian (18.7 to 15.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Amongst the Acanthisittidae family, Kuiornis indicator is most closely related to the living rifleman.
rejected.quote: Amongst acanthisittids it is most closely related to the living rifleman
